get.summary: Whether the API and its database are working
The relays apps connect through and the oldest app version still served

200.description: The network settings. Cacheable for five minutes; apps keep the last copy they read for when the API cannot be reached.

429.description: Too many requests from this address.

post.summary: A one-time value for a device to sign before it registers
post.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or the Mac app's OAuth token from a sign-in in the last ten minutes, which it uses only to register its host.

200.description: The challenge, valid for two minutes.

post.summary: Add a device to your account, or update it
post.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or the Mac app's OAuth token from a sign-in in the last ten minutes, which it uses only to register its host.

200.description: The device was already yours and is updated.

get.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or a request signed by a host on the account.

delete.summary: Take one of your devices off your account, from the phone, the web app or the app on one of your hosts
delete.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or a request signed by a host on the account.

204.description: The device is no longer on your account.

post.summary: Rename one of your devices or hosts, from the phone, the web app or the app on one of your hosts
post.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or a request signed by a host on the account.

200.description: The device under its new name. Every device hears device.changed.

404.description: None of your devices has that key.

put.summary: Deliver this phone's notifications to a push token
put.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

200.description: The token is stored, replacing the phone's earlier one. A token another phone had moves to this one.

400.description: The challenge is unknown, used or expired, or this server does not deliver to that app or APNs environment.

403.description: The signature does not prove the phone holds its key.

404.description: None of your phones has that key.

delete.summary: Stop delivering notifications to this phone
delete.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

204.description: The phone has no push token, whether or not it had one.

404.description: None of your phones has that key.

post.summary: A ticket for this phone to join one of your hosts without a code
post.description: The phone's or the web app's sign-in, or a request signed by a host on the account.

200.description: The ticket, good for ten minutes. The host still asks its owner before letting the phone in.

404.description: None of your phones has that key, or none of your hosts has the host's.

429.description: More than 10 tickets for this phone in a minute.

post.summary: Start signing in a host that has no browser, such as a server reached over SSH

201.description: The codes, good for ten minutes. The host shows the user code and asks every interval seconds whether it was approved.

429.description: Too many sign-ins from this address.

post.summary: Whether the person approved this host yet

200.description: Pending, or approved with the account and a challenge to sign.

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

429.description: Asked more often than the interval allows.

post.summary: Register the approved host on the account, proving it holds its key

200.description: The host was already on the account and is updated. The code is used up.

201.description: The host is on the account. The code is used up.

400.description: The challenge is unknown, used or expired.

403.description: The signature does not prove the host holds its key.

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

409.description: The key is registered to another account, or as a phone.

get.summary: The host waiting behind a user code, to check before approving it
get.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

delete.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

204.description: Refused. The host hears the code is gone.

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

post.summary: Add the waiting host to your account
post.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

204.description: Approved. The host finishes on its next ask.

403.description: The sign-in was not verified again within the error's reverifyWithinMinutes (message reverify).

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

post.summary: Add the waiting host to your account from the app on another of your hosts, which read the code over SSH
post.description: Only a request signed by a host on the account.

200.description: Approved, naming the host. It finishes on its next ask.

404.description: The code is unknown, was refused, or has expired.

get.summary: One connection per device that pushes account events as they happen
get.description: A WebSocket. The device proves who it is in its first message, since browsers cannot set headers on one. `send` is what the device sends; `receive` is what the server sends.

101.description: The connection is open. The server sends a challenge; the device answers with hello within 10 seconds. Its close codes are LiveCloseCode.

429.description: Too many connections from this address.

get.summary: Whether your account is in use or waiting to be deleted
get.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

200.description: The account's status. A deleted account still answers, so an app can offer to restore it.

delete.summary: Delete your account and take every device off it
delete.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

202.description: The account is deleted here and its devices revoked; the sign-in is deleted in Clerk at deletesAt unless the account is restored first. Repeating the call answers the same way. Revoking Sign in with Apple is tried once, and the deletion goes ahead whether or not it works.

400.description: The body is not a valid AccountDeletionRequest.

403.description: The sign-in was not verified again within the error's reverifyWithinMinutes (message reverify).

post.summary: Take back a deletion before it is final
post.description: Only the phone's and the web app's sign-ins; the Mac app's OAuth token is refused with 403.

200.description: The account is in use again, with no devices on it; each signs in again. Restoring an account in use changes nothing.

404.description: The sign-in is already deleted in Clerk, so the account can no longer be restored.

get.summary: The name, email and picture of the account a host is on
get.description: Only a request signed by a host on the account.

200.description: The profile, read from the account's sign-in.

post.summary: Clerk telling the API a user was deleted in its dashboard
post.description: Called by Clerk, signed with Svix's headers.

204.description: Handled, or not an event the API acts on.

401.description: The Svix signature is missing, wrong or too old.

503.description: The API has no webhook secret, so it accepts no webhooks.

Account.description: Whether the signed-in account is in use or waiting to be deleted.

deletesAt.description: Only while deleting: when the account is deleted for good unless restored first.

restorableDays.description: How many days a deleted account can still be restored: deletesAt is this long after the deletion.

AccountDeletion.description: Every device is revoked and every token refused from the moment this is answered, except to read or restore the account. Signing in again before deletesAt can restore it.

deletesAt.description: When the sign-in is deleted for good and the account can no longer be restored.

AccountDeletionRequest.description: What the phone may send when it deletes an account. The body can be left out.

appleAuthorizationCode.description: A code Sign in with Apple gave the phone moments ago. The server trades it for a token and revokes that, so Apple stops treating the person as signed in to Sikemux.

AccountDeletionStatus.description: Deleting while the account can still be restored, until the server deletes the sign-in in Clerk at deletesAt; deleted once Clerk has.

AccountEvent.description: Something changed on the account. Events carry keys, never names: a device rereads the lists it shows over HTTP.

key.description: The device the event is about. Absent from account.deleted.

role.description: That device's role. Absent from account.deleted.

AccountProfile.description: The name, email and picture the account signed in with, for a host to show who it belongs to.

AccountStatus.description: Active, or deleting: deleted on request and still restorable until deletesAt.

ApiError.description: The body of every response that is not a success.

ApnsEnvironment.description: Which of Apple's push servers issued an iOS token: sandbox for builds run from Xcode, production for TestFlight and the App Store.

ApprovedHost.description: The host a sign-in code belonged to, once approved.

AppVersion.description: A semantic version, such as 0.5.0 or 0.6.0-nightly.3.

Challenge.description: A one-time value a device signs to prove it holds its key.

Channel.description: Which build a host runs. Dev, nightly and stable cores are separate hosts.

ChannelVersions.description: An app older than its channel's version, compared as semantic versions, must update before it connects.

DeviceKey.description: A device's iroh public key: 32 bytes of Ed25519, in lowercase hex.

DeviceRegistration.description: Adds a device to the signed-in account, or updates it if it is already there. The signature is the device key's Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-register|<nonce>|<user id>|<key>`.

DeviceRename.description: What a device or host is called on the account, everywhere it is shown.

DeviceRole.description: A host is a core people connect to, such as a Mac. A client connects to hosts, such as a phone.

message.description: Written for whoever reads the logs. Apps show their own words for each code.

requestId.description: The same as the response's x-request-id header, and how the server's logs find this request.

reverifyWithinMinutes.description: Only with reverify_required: how recently the person must have proved their first factor.

EventId.description: An account event's place in the log. Later events have larger ids.

Health.description: Whether the API can serve requests, and which build is answering.

version.description: The commit the running build was made from, or "dev".

HostSignIn.description: What the host shows and keeps while its person approves it from a device already signed in.

verificationUrl.description: Where the person approves this host by typing the code it shows. It never carries the code, so a link alone cannot approve anything.

interval.description: How many seconds the host waits between asks whether it was approved.

HostSignInCode.description: The secret a host holds while it waits to be signed in: 32 random bytes in lowercase hex. Only the host ever sees it.

HostSignInFinish.description: Registers the approved host. The signature is the host key's, over the same text a DeviceRegistration signs, with the account from HostSignInState.

HostSignInStart.description: A host with no browser asks to be signed in. It proves its key only when it finishes, once it knows the account.

HostSignInState.description: Pending until the person approves. Approved carries the account and a fresh challenge, which the host signs as it would a DeviceRegistration and sends back in HostSignInFinish.

account.description: Only once approved: the Clerk user id of the account that approved.

nonce.description: Only once approved: a challenge good for two minutes.

HostSignInUserCode.description: What the host shows its person, who types it on a device already signed in. Eight consonants in two groups of four.

JoinRequest.description: Which host on the account the phone wants to join.

JoinTicket.description: The server's word that a phone and a host are on the same account. The phone hands it to the host over ALPN sikemux/join/1, and the host checks it without calling the server, then still asks its owner. The signature is the server's Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-join|v1|<keyId>|<account>|<host>|<phone>|<issuedAt>|<expiresAt>`, with the times in decimal, followed by `|<via>|<viaName>` when the ticket has them.

keyId.description: Which of the server's signing keys signed it: prod-1 in production, dev-1 for a local API.

account.description: The Clerk user id of the account the phone and the host are on.

issuedAt.description: When the server signed it, in unix seconds.

expiresAt.description: When it stops being good, in unix seconds: ten minutes after issuedAt.

via.description: The host that added the joining app to the account, when a host did, so the host it joins can say which.

viaName.description: What the account calls the host in via.

LiveAck.description: Every event up to and including id is handled.

LiveApp.description: The build that opened the connection, for the server's logs.

LiveAuth.description: Web only: a fresh Clerk session token for the same user, sent before ready.authExpiresAt.

LiveBye.description: The server is restarting and closes with LiveCloseCode restarting after it. Reconnect no sooner than reconnectAfterMs.

LiveChallenge.description: The server's first message on every connection: a one-time value the device's hello answers.

LiveCloseCode.description: Why the server closed a live connection, as the WebSocket close code.

oneOf.title: badMessage
oneOf.description: The device sent something the protocol does not allow. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: unauthenticated
oneOf.description: The hello did not prove who the device is, or the web app's sign-in expired.

oneOf.title: revoked
oneOf.description: The device is no longer on the account, after a revoked message. Do not reconnect.

oneOf.title: helloTimeout
oneOf.description: No hello came within 10 seconds of the challenge. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: replaced
oneOf.description: A newer connection for the same device took over. Reconnecting at once would push that one off.

oneOf.title: overLimit
oneOf.description: Over a limit: more messages a second than allowed, too many failed hellos from this key or address in a minute, or too many connections for the account. Wait at least 30 seconds, since the limits count over a minute.

oneOf.title: serverError
oneOf.description: Something failed on the server. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: restarting
oneOf.description: The server is restarting, after a bye message. Reconnect no sooner than its reconnectAfterMs.

oneOf.title: overloaded
oneOf.description: The server has too many connections, or the device stopped reading. Reconnect with backoff.

LiveDeviceMessage.description: What a device or the web app sends on a live connection.

LiveEvents.description: Events the device has not acknowledged yet, oldest first. Delivery is at least once.

LiveHello.description: The device's first message, answering the challenge. Hosts send key and signature; clients send key, signature and their Clerk session token; the web app sends only its token. The signature is the device key's Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-live|<nonce>|<key>`.

LiveLeave.description: Hosts and clients only: take this device off its account. The server answers with revoked (signed_out).

LivePush.description: Hosts only: deliver a notification to one of the account's phones. The blob is sealed on the host with a key only that phone has, and the server passes it on unread. The server answers with pushed.

collapseId.description: Opaque to the server. A later push with the same collapseId replaces or clears the notification this one shows.

blob.description: The sealed notification, in standard base64.

expiresAt.description: After this the push is worth nothing, so the server drops it rather than deliver it late.

LivePushed.description: The answer to a host's push, carrying the push's ref.

LiveReady.description: The hello was accepted. Events after the device's cursor follow.

latest.description: The account's newest event id, or 0 when it has none.

heartbeatMs.description: How often the server pings. A device that hears nothing for twice as long reconnects.

authExpiresAt.description: Web only: send a fresh token in an auth message before this.

LiveReset.description: Some events after the device's cursor are no longer kept. Clients reread their lists; the events that follow are still every kept event after the cursor.

LiveRevoked.description: This device is no longer on the account. The server closes with LiveCloseCode revoked after it.

LiveRole.description: Who opens a live connection. A host or a client proves its device key; the web app is not a device and shows only its sign-in.

LiveServerMessage.description: What the server sends on a live connection.

MinimumVersions.description: The oldest version of each app the server works with, by platform. Dev builds are never too old.

Network.description: How hosts and phones reach each other, and the oldest app the server still serves. Apps read it when they start, so changing either needs no app release.

relays.description: The relays to use, best first. A host connects to every one; a phone dials a host through the relay the host says it is on.

PendingHost.description: The host waiting behind a user code, for the person to check before approving it.

requestedAt.description: When the host asked to be signed in.

requestedFrom.description: The address the host asked from, as the server saw it, or null when it is not known.

requestedNear.description: Where requestedFrom is, as far as the server's IP database knows: the country, then the network's owner, such as `Germany · Hetzner Online`. Null when it does not know.

removedAt.description: Only for a host once removed from this account: when it was. It can come back only through a code approved like this.

PushApp.description: Which build of the phone app the token belongs to. Each has its own Firebase project and bundle id, and an API serves only one of them.

PushKind.description: alert shows a notification. clear removes one shown before with the same collapseId, and is delivered at a lower priority.

PushPlatform.description: Which service delivers to the phone: Apple's push service, or Firebase Cloud Messaging.

PushRef.description: A number the host picks for each push, so it can match the server's answer to it.

PushResult.description: What became of a push. sent: the platform accepted it. no_token: the phone has notifications off. not_allowed: the target is not a phone on the sender's account. throttled: over a limit, dropped. expired: its expiresAt had passed. not_set_up: this server cannot reach the phone's platform. failed: the platform refused it or could not be reached.

PushTokenRegistration.description: Where the phone wants its notifications delivered. The signature is the phone's device key's Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-push|<nonce>|<key>|<sha256 of the token, lowercase hex>`, so no other sign-in on the account can redirect the phone's notifications.

token.description: The token the platform gave the app: the native APNs or FCM token, never an Expo push token.

apnsEnvironment.description: Required when platform is apns, and absent otherwise.

enabled.description: Whether the server has a token for this phone.

url.description: The relay's HTTPS address, such as https://relay.sikemux.com/.

region.description: Where the relay runs, for logs and settings screens.

quicPort.description: The UDP port of the relay's QUIC address discovery, or null when it has none.

RevokeReason.description: Why a device left its account: removed from another device or the web, signed out on the device itself, or the account was deleted.

Sealed.description: What the host sealed for the share's viewers: a 12-byte nonce, then AES-256-GCM ciphertext and tag, in unpadded base64url. The key lives only in the share's link, so the server cannot read it.

ShareAnswer.description: Host only: the sealed answer to one viewer's question.

ShareAnswered.description: To a viewer: the host's sealed answer to one of its questions.

ShareAsk.description: Viewer only: a sealed question for the host, such as the chat's turns before some event or a picture pasted into it. The host answers with answer.

ShareAsked.description: To the host: a viewer's sealed question. Answer it with answer, naming the viewer.

ShareAuth.description: Viewer only: a fresh Clerk token for the same user, sent before ready.authExpiresAt.

ShareBye.description: The server is restarting and closes with ShareCloseCode restarting after it. Reconnect no sooner than reconnectAfterMs.

ShareChallenge.description: The server's first message on every share connection: a one-time value a host's hello signs.

ShareClientMessage.description: What a host or a viewer sends on a share connection.

ShareClose.description: Host only: end a share for good. Its viewers are told it was stopped.

ShareCloseCode.description: Why the server closed a share connection, as the WebSocket close code.

oneOf.title: badMessage
oneOf.description: Something the protocol does not allow was sent. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: unauthenticated
oneOf.description: The hello did not prove who is connecting, or the viewer's sign-in expired.

oneOf.title: notFound
oneOf.description: No share has this id. Do not reconnect.

oneOf.title: helloTimeout
oneOf.description: No hello came within 10 seconds of the challenge. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: replaced
oneOf.description: A newer connection for the same host took over.

oneOf.title: ended
oneOf.description: The share ended, after an ended message. Do not reconnect.

oneOf.title: overLimit
oneOf.description: Over a limit: too many messages, viewers or failed hellos. Wait at least 30 seconds.

oneOf.title: serverError
oneOf.description: Something failed on the server. Reconnect with backoff.

oneOf.title: restarting
oneOf.description: The server is restarting, after a bye message. Reconnect no sooner than its reconnectAfterMs.

oneOf.title: overloaded
oneOf.description: The server has too many connections, or the connection stopped reading. Reconnect with backoff.

ShareEnded.description: The share ended. The server closes a viewer's connection with ShareCloseCode ended after it.

ShareEndReason.description: Why a share ended: the host stopped it or its chat ended, or it ran past its expiry.

ShareFrame.description: One sealed frame of a share. A snapshot holds the whole chat as it stands, so a viewer starts over from it and the frames before it are no longer needed.

ShareFrames.description: To a viewer: frames in order. One with snapshot set replaces everything before it.

ShareHello.description: The first message on a share connection. A host sends its key and its Ed25519 signature over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-share|<nonce>|<key>`. A viewer sends the share it wants, the proof its link holds and the last frame it holds, if any, and signs in with a Clerk token from the web app or the phone, or, on a Mac, with the host's key and its Ed25519 signature over `sikemux-share-viewer|<nonce>|<key>`.

ShareHost.description: To a viewer: the sharing host connected or went away. Questions wait for it.

ShareId.description: A shared chat's id: 16 random bytes the host picks, in unpadded base64url.

ShareOpen.description: Host only: start a share. The server answers opened or refused. Hosts on 0.5.3 and earlier send no viewers check, and their shares are open to anyone signed in who has the link.

ShareOpened.description: To the host: the share is open and viewers may join.

SharePublish.description: Host only: the share's next frame, for every viewer now and later.

ShareReady.description: The hello was accepted. A viewer is sent the frames it does not hold next, from the latest snapshot on.

expiresAt.description: Viewer only: when the share ends.

hostOnline.description: Viewer only: whether the sharing host is connected.

authExpiresAt.description: Viewer only: send a fresh token in an auth message before this.

ShareRefusal.description: Why the server would not open a share: the account has as many open as it may, the id is taken, or the expiry is not between now and seven days from now.

ShareRefused.description: To the host: the share was not opened.

ShareRole.description: A host publishes its shared chats; a viewer watches one.

ShareSeq.description: A frame's place in its share. The host numbers frames from 1, one higher each time.

ShareServerMessage.description: What the server sends on a share connection.

ShareViewerCheck.description: The lowercase hex SHA-256 of a share's ShareViewerProof bytes, which the host gives the server so it can check viewers without learning the proof.

ShareViewerId.description: One viewer's connection, as the server names it to the host.

ShareViewerProof.description: What a share's link proves to the server, so only someone holding the link takes a viewer's place: HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the link's 32-byte key over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-share-viewer|v1|<share id>`, in unpadded base64url. It cannot be turned back into the key.

ShareViewers.description: To the host: how many viewers a share has now.

ShareWantsSnapshot.description: To the host: the server let go of the share's frames, so the next frame it publishes must be a snapshot.

session.description: A Clerk sign-in: a session token from the phone or the web app, or the Mac app's OAuth access token.

host.description: `Authorization: SikemuxHost <key>.<time>.<signature>`: a host on the account signs each request with its key. `time` is the request's Unix time in seconds, within a minute of the server's, and `signature` the Ed25519 signature in hex over the UTF-8 text `sikemux-host-request|<METHOD>|<path and query>|<time>|<lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body>`. The server takes each signature once.
